place:mtn:zagros_mountains.what: The long wall of folded ridges between the Mesopotamian plain and the Iranian plateau.
place:mtn:zagros_mountains.why: For 5,000 years it was the frontier between lowland empires (Sumer, Babylon, Rome, the Ottomans) and highland ones (Elam, Persia), crossed at a few gaps like the Persian Gates.

place:mtn:taurus_mountains.what: The mountain arc along Anatolia's south coast.
place:mtn:taurus_mountains.why: It walled Anatolia off from Syria; armies from Alexander to the Crusaders squeezed through the Cilician Gates, and it was the Byzantine-Arab frontier for 300 years.

place:mtn:hindu_kush.what: The high range across Afghanistan, westward continuation of the Pamirs.
place:mtn:hindu_kush.why: Every invasion of India from the northwest, from Alexander to Babur, had to cross it, usually by the Khyber; its name is often read as 'killer of Hindus' for the slaves who died crossing.

place:mtn:pamir_mountains.what: The 'Roof of the World', where the Himalaya, Hindu Kush, Tian Shan and Kunlun knot together.
place:mtn:pamir_mountains.why: The Silk Road had to cross it between the Tarim Basin and Bactria, and in the 1800s it was where the British and Russian empires nearly touched in the Great Game.

place:mtn:himalayas.what: The world's highest range, along the northern edge of the Indian subcontinent.
place:mtn:himalayas.why: It sealed India off from China for most of history, so the two civilisations met mainly by sea or through Central Asia, and its snowmelt feeds the Indus, Ganges and Brahmaputra.

place:plateau:tibetan_plateau.what: The highest and largest plateau on Earth, averaging over 4,500 m.
place:plateau:tibetan_plateau.why: It is Asia's water tower (the Yellow, Yangtze, Mekong, Indus and Brahmaputra start here), and it let a thin, high kingdom rival Tang China in the 600s to 800s.

place:mtn:alps.what: The great arc of mountains across south-central Europe.
place:mtn:alps.why: Hannibal crossed it to invade Italy, and for 2,000 years the passes (Brenner, Great St Bernard) decided how Germany and Italy connected.

place:mtn:pyrenees.what: The range between France and Spain.
place:mtn:pyrenees.why: It kept Iberia half apart from Europe: the Umayyad advance stopped beyond it, and Charlemagne's rearguard died at Roncevaux.

place:mtn:caucasus_mountains.what: The range between the Black and Caspian seas.
place:mtn:caucasus_mountains.why: It was the classic barrier against steppe nomads; only the Darial Gorge and the Derbent coast road crossed it, both fortified since antiquity.

place:mtn:ural_mountains.what: Low, old mountains running north-south through Russia.
place:mtn:ural_mountains.why: The conventional line between Europe and Asia, though so low that nomads and Russian traders crossed it easily; Russia's conquest of Siberia started just beyond.

place:mtn:tian_shan.what: The 'Heavenly Mountains' of Central Asia, between Kazakhstan and the Tarim Basin.
place:mtn:tian_shan.why: The Silk Road split to run along its north and south feet, and the Dzungarian Gate at its east end was the nomads' highway into the west.

place:mtn:carpathian_mountains.what: The mountain arc around the Hungarian plain.
place:mtn:carpathian_mountains.why: It made the Hungarian plain a fortress-pasture where Huns, Avars and Magyars could settle, and its Iron Gates gorge controls the Danube.

place:mtn:balkan_mountains.what: The range across Bulgaria that gave the whole peninsula its name.
place:mtn:balkan_mountains.why: Its passes were the gates of Constantinople from the north; Bulgars, Byzantines and Russians fought over them for 1,300 years.

place:mtn:dinaric_alps.what: The rugged limestone mountains along the eastern Adriatic.
place:mtn:dinaric_alps.why: Their karst made the western Balkans hard to conquer and easy to fragment, from Illyrian tribes to Yugoslavia.

place:mtn:elburz_mountains.what: The range along the Caspian's south shore, crowned by Damavand.
place:mtn:elburz_mountains.why: It split Iran into a wet Caspian strip and the dry plateau, and sheltered the Caspian Gates route that every army into Iran or Central Asia used.

place:mtn:kopet_dag.what: The range on today's Iran-Turkmenistan border.
place:mtn:kopet_dag.why: It marked the edge of settled Iran against the Turkmen steppe and the Karakum; Parthia was born at its foot.

place:mtn:mount_lebanon_range.why: Its cedars built Egyptian ships, Solomon's temple and Phoenician fleets, and it sheltered minorities like the Maronites and Druze.

place:mtn:atlas_mountains.what: The ranges across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.
place:mtn:atlas_mountains.why: They separate the Mediterranean coast from the Sahara and gave Amazigh peoples a refuge from Carthage, Rome and the Arabs.

place:mtn:ethiopian_highlands.what: The high, rainy plateau of Ethiopia and Eritrea.
place:mtn:ethiopian_highlands.why: Source of the Blue Nile flood that fed Egypt, and a natural fortress that kept Aksum and Ethiopia independent for nearly all of history.

place:mtn:qinling.what: The east-west range in central China.
place:mtn:qinling.why: It splits China into the dry wheat north and the wet rice south, and protected the Wei valley capitals Xi'an and Chang'an.

place:mtn:sulaiman_mountains.what: The range between the Indus plain and Afghanistan.
place:mtn:sulaiman_mountains.why: It forms the western wall of the Indus valley; the Bolan Pass through it was the southern invasion route into India.

place:mtn:pindus.what: The mountain spine of mainland Greece.
place:mtn:pindus.why: It cut Greece into small valleys, one reason the Greeks lived in hundreds of separate city-states.

place:mtn:western_ghats.what: The escarpment along India's west coast.
place:mtn:western_ghats.why: It catches the monsoon, making the Malabar coast the pepper country that drew Romans, Arabs and the Portuguese.

place:mtn:andes.what: The longest continental range, along western South America.
place:mtn:andes.why: The Inca ran the largest empire of the Americas along its spine with road networks and terraced valleys.

place:region:anatolia.what: The peninsula of Asian Turkey, a high plateau rimmed by mountains.
place:region:anatolia.why: The land bridge between Europe and Asia: Hittites, Persians, Romans, Byzantines, Seljuks and Ottomans all built empires on it.

place:desert:sahara.what: The largest hot desert, across North Africa.
place:desert:sahara.why: It split Africa into a Mediterranean world and a sub-Saharan one until camels (from about 300 CE) made the gold and salt caravans possible.

place:desert:syrian_desert.what: The steppe-desert between the Levant and the Euphrates.
place:desert:syrian_desert.why: It pushed Fertile Crescent traffic into an arc around its edge and made oasis cities like Palmyra rich from the caravans across it.

place:desert:rub_al_khali.what: The 'Empty Quarter', the largest sand sea on Earth, in southern Arabia.
place:desert:rub_al_khali.why: It forced the incense road to hug the Hejaz mountains, which is why Mecca and Medina sat on the main route.

place:mtn:hejaz_mountains.what: The mountains along Arabia's Red Sea coast.
place:mtn:hejaz_mountains.why: The incense road ran along their foot, through the Hejaz towns of Mecca and Medina where Islam began.

place:desert:gobi_desert.what: The cold desert of Mongolia and northern China.
place:desert:gobi_desert.why: It separated the Mongolian steppe from China; the Great Wall and the Hexi Corridor run along its southern edge.

place:basin:tarim_basin.what: The enclosed basin north of Tibet, filled by the Taklamakan desert.
place:basin:tarim_basin.why: Its rim of oasis cities (Kashgar, Khotan, Turfan) carried the Silk Road, Buddhism and paper between China and the west.

place:desert:karakum_desert.why: Merv, once among the world's largest cities, grew on an oasis at its edge before the Mongols destroyed it in 1221.

place:desert:kyzyl_kum.what: The red-sand desert between the Amu Darya and Syr Darya.
place:desert:kyzyl_kum.why: Bukhara and Samarkand sat on rivers along its edge, at the heart of Transoxiana.

place:desert:thar_desert.what: The Great Indian Desert of Rajasthan.
place:desert:thar_desert.why: It funnelled invaders from the northwest towards the Punjab and Delhi rather than straight into the Gangetic heartland.

place:desert:nubian_desert.what: The desert east of the Nile in Sudan.
place:desert:nubian_desert.why: Its gold made Nubia ('Nub' = gold) rich, and Egypt crossed it to reach Kush.

place:desert:negev.why: Nabataean caravan towns crossed it on the incense road from Petra to Gaza.

place:plain:pontic_caspian_steppe.what: The grassland from the Danube to the Urals north of the Black Sea.
place:plain:pontic_caspian_steppe.why: The western end of the steppe highway: Indo-Europeans, Scythians, Huns, Khazars, Cumans and the Golden Horde all rode out of it.

place:plain:kazakh_steppe.what: The vast dry grassland of Kazakhstan.
place:plain:kazakh_steppe.why: The middle of the Eurasian steppe corridor that let horse nomads move from Mongolia to Hungary.

place:plain:north_european_plain.what: The lowland from the Netherlands to Russia.
place:plain:north_european_plain.why: Few natural barriers: armies from Napoleon to Hitler crossed it, which is why Poland's borders kept moving.

place:plain:north_china_plain.what: The flat loess-filled plain of the lower Yellow River.
place:plain:north_china_plain.why: China's original heartland and grain base, and the river's flooding over it has killed millions.

place:plateau:loess_plateau.what: Deep wind-blown silt hills on the middle Yellow River.
place:plateau:loess_plateau.why: Its soft, fertile soil fed early Chinese farming and gives the Yellow River its silt and its name.

place:plain:indo_gangetic_plain.what: The plain of the Indus and Ganges across northern India and Pakistan.
place:plain:indo_gangetic_plain.why: Home to the Harappans and later to Maurya, Gupta and Mughal power; for 2,500 years whoever held it held India.

place:plateau:deccan_plateau.why: It kept southern India politically separate from the north for long stretches, and the Mughals wore themselves out conquering it.

place:plateau:mongolian_plateau.why: The homeland of the Xiongnu, the Turks and the Mongols, whose horses could only be raised on grass like this.

place:plain:sahel.what: The semi-arid belt along the Sahara's southern edge.
place:plain:sahel.why: Ghana, Mali and Songhai rose along it, where caravans from the desert met the farmers and gold of the south.

place:valley:great_rift_valley.what: The tectonic rift running from Syria to Mozambique.
place:valley:great_rift_valley.why: Many of the oldest human fossils come from it, and its lakes and highlands shaped East Africa's peoples.

place:valley:fergana_valley.what: A fertile valley enclosed by the Tian Shan.
place:valley:fergana_valley.why: Famous for the 'heavenly horses' that drew Han China into Central Asia in 104 BCE; it remains one of Central Asia's most populous places.

place:basin:sichuan_basin.what: A fertile mountain-ringed basin in southwest China.
place:basin:sichuan_basin.why: Its walls made it a natural kingdom (Shu); the Dujiangyan irrigation of 256 BCE turned it into Qin's granary for uniting China.

place:river:nile.what: The river through northeast Africa, longest in the world.
place:river:nile.why: Its yearly flood made Egypt possible; a narrow green strip in desert fed one of history's longest-lived states.

place:river:tigris.why: Nineveh, Ctesiphon and Baghdad all stood on it.

place:river:euphrates.why: Ur, Babylon and Mari stood on it, and it was the Roman-Persian frontier for 600 years.

place:river:indus.why: The Harappan civilisation grew along it; it gave India its name, and was Alexander's eastern limit.

place:river:ganges.what: The holy river of northern India.
place:river:ganges.why: The heartland of Magadha, the Buddha and the Mauryas, and still India's densest farmland.

place:river:yellow_river.what: China's northern great river, named for its silt.
place:river:yellow_river.why: The cradle of Chinese civilisation and 'China's Sorrow': its course shifts have killed millions and toppled dynasties.

place:river:yangtze.what: China's longest river, across the middle of the country.
place:river:yangtze.why: The rice-rich lower Yangtze became China's economic centre after about 1000 CE, and the river was the north-south line of many divided eras.

place:river:danube.what: The river from the Black Forest to the Black Sea.
place:river:danube.why: The Roman frontier for 400 years and the road into Europe for nomads and Ottomans alike.

place:river:rhine.what: The river from the Alps to the North Sea.
place:river:rhine.why: The Roman frontier with Germania and later the long contested line between France and Germany; Europe's busiest river trade route.

place:river:volga.what: Europe's longest river, flowing to the Caspian.
place:river:volga.why: The Viking-Khazar fur and silver route, the seat of the Golden Horde (Sarai), and Russia's spine.

place:river:dnieper.what: The river through Ukraine to the Black Sea.
place:river:dnieper.why: The 'route from the Varangians to the Greeks' that built Kyivan Rus.

place:river:amu_darya.what: The Oxus, from the Pamirs to the old Aral Sea.
place:river:amu_darya.why: The ancient line between Iran and Turan; Bactria and Khwarazm flourished along it.

place:river:syr_darya.what: The Jaxartes, from the Tian Shan to the Aral Sea.
place:river:syr_darya.why: The northern edge of the settled world for Alexander and the Arabs; beyond it lay the steppe.

place:river:niger.what: West Africa's great river, looping through the Sahel.
place:river:niger.why: Timbuktu, Gao and Djenne grew on its bend, where desert caravans met river boats.

place:river:mekong.what: The river from Tibet to the South China Sea.
place:river:mekong.why: Angkor's rice and fish came from its flood pulse via the Tonle Sap.

place:sea:mediterranean_sea.what: The almost-enclosed sea between Europe, Africa and Asia.
place:sea:mediterranean_sea.why: Calm, tideless and ringed with harbours, it let Phoenicians, Greeks, Romans and Venetians knit three continents together.

place:sea:black_sea.what: The inland sea north of Anatolia.
place:sea:black_sea.why: Its grain fed Athens and Constantinople, and it connects the steppe rivers to the Mediterranean through the Bosporus.

place:sea:aegean_sea.what: The island-scattered sea between Greece and Anatolia.
place:sea:aegean_sea.why: Islands in sight of each other made it the school of Greek seafaring and the stage for Troy, Salamis and the Delian League.

place:sea:red_sea.what: The narrow sea between Africa and Arabia.
place:sea:red_sea.why: The sea lane from India to Egypt and the Mediterranean, opened by monsoon sailing and later by the Suez Canal.

place:gulf:persian_gulf.what: The sea between Arabia and Iran.
place:gulf:persian_gulf.why: From Dilmun to Hormuz to oil tankers it has linked Mesopotamia to India and the world.

place:sea:caspian_sea.what: The largest lake on Earth, below sea level.
place:sea:caspian_sea.why: A closed sea that steered steppe traffic around its north (the Volga) and south (the Derbent and Caspian gates).

place:sea:arabian_sea.what: The northwest Indian Ocean between Arabia and India.
place:sea:arabian_sea.why: Monsoon winds that reverse each season let ships cross it directly, the engine of Indian Ocean trade since Roman times.

place:sea:south_china_sea.what: The sea between southern China, Vietnam and the Philippines.
place:sea:south_china_sea.why: The maritime silk road ran through it from Guangzhou to Malacca.

place:sea:baltic_sea.what: The brackish sea of northern Europe.
place:sea:baltic_sea.why: The Hanseatic League's trading lake and Sweden's 17th-century empire.

place:sea:north_sea.what: The shallow sea between Britain and the continent.
place:sea:north_sea.why: Viking raids, the herring trade and the Dutch and English navies all came out of it.

place:sea:sea_of_azov.what: The shallow sea north of the Black Sea.
place:sea:sea_of_azov.why: Greek colonies traded steppe grain and fish here; the Don flows into it.

place:lake:baikal.what: The world's deepest and oldest lake, in Siberia.
place:lake:baikal.why: It marked the northern edge of the Mongol world and was the hardest obstacle on the Trans-Siberian Railway.

place:lake:victoria.why: Long sought as the source of the Nile, and its shores held the Buganda kingdom.
